title: Pointers: the basics, with structs, with maps and slices

videos.script: Lesson 22 ended on a rule. Every argument is a copy, so a function cannot change your variable. This lesson is the way around it. {{amp}} An ampersand gives you the address of a variable. A star follows an address back to the value. Hand a function the address, and it can write into your variable. {{nil}} A pointer can also point at nothing. Follow that one, and the program stops. And unlike C, you cannot do arithmetic on a Go pointer at all. {{structs}} Then structs, where pointers are everywhere. A dot follows the pointer for you, and new makes a value and hands you its address. {{maps}} Last, the places a pointer cannot go. You cannot take the address of a map element. And a pointer into a slice gets left behind when append moves the slice. By the end you will know when a function needs your address, and when a copy is the better choice.
